title: Cross-experiment analysis of completed gbdt cells (US sweep #107 snapshot + standalone)
snapshot_caveat: PARTIAL SWEEP. The 57-cell US sweep (#107) is mid-run (grinding russell1000 cells ~5h each). This analysis covers ONLY the 12 sweep cells with a complete metrics.json as of 2026-05-29 (~12 of 57 sweep cells, ~21%), plus 4 standalone H=25 / broad-universe cells for cross-market context. russell1000_up_20pct_5d_dd10pct was mid-build (no metrics.json) and is EXCLUDED. Patterns below are provisional and weighted toward short-horizon nasdaq/sp500 cells; the russell1000 and longer-horizon coverage is thin (1 russell cell, 1 nasdaq 100d cell with no test window).
metrics_note: R-precision is per-day variable-K weighted (sum positives_caught / sum R(d)); panel-invariant, the standard cross-cell metric. AUC reported eval+test. Lift = R-prec / base_rate, shown here as a numeric field for machine consumption only — NOT rendered as a table column in the memo (CLAUDE.md reporting convention). base_rate columns are present so readers compute lift on demand.
compound_rule: AUC in [0.45,0.55] AND R-prec lift <1.2x -> null; AUC in [0.45,0.55] AND lift >1.5x -> hidden top-tail; lift in [1.2,1.5] in null AUC band -> ambiguous; AUC>0.55 -> discriminating.

key_findings.eval_to_test_auc_decay_systemic: Every sweep cell loses AUC eval->test (dAUC always negative, range -0.022 to -0.144). The decay is systemic, not cell-specific. Magnitude scales with horizon within the +10% family: 5d -0.044, 10d -0.127, 25d -0.144 (collapses into the [0.45,0.55] null band on test), 100d has zero test rows. The +20% cells decay far less (-0.022 to -0.072) and stay strongly discriminating on test.
key_findings.horizon_effect: Short horizons (5d, 10d) are the cleanest. R-prec lift is highest at 5d and declines monotonically with horizon. By 25d the nasdaq +10% cell is on the edge of null on test; the 100d cell is null on eval (AUC 0.488) and has no test window at all (H=100 consumes the entire 100-row per-ticker test segment).
key_findings.threshold_effect: Higher thresholds (rarer events) give HIGHER R-prec lift but on a much smaller base rate. sp500 +20%/5d: base 0.3%, lift 23.7x on test; nasdaq +40%/10d: base 0.2%, lift 7.6x. The absolute R-precision (~0.15-0.21) is modest but the top picks concentrate the rare event strongly. +10% cells have lower lift (5-11x at 5d) on a larger base (3-4%).
key_findings.universe_effect: sp500 (larger panel, ~486 names) shows the strongest lift at matched thresholds (more positives/day -> deeper cross-section for F14 rank/z features). russell1000 (1 cell only) is comparable to nasdaq at +10%/5d (lift 5.1x test). nasdaq sits between. nifty500 standalone (_176, +30%/50d) lift 3.2x test corroborates the broad-universe-helps thesis.
key_findings.100d_no_test_window: nasdaq100 +10%/100d produced n_rows_test=0: the H=100 horizon eats the entire 100-row test segment per ticker, so test metrics are empty and eval AUC (0.488) is null. Long horizons need a larger per-ticker test allocation than the 800/400/200/100 split provides. This is a methodology limitation to flag for the sweep design.
key_findings.nifty500_cross_market: _176 nifty500 (+30%/50d) hit R-prec lift 4.36x eval / 3.17x test with aggressive FS (279->39). Exceeds nifty50 _147 H=25 (~2.0-2.2x), consistent with broader-universe cross-section helping. nifty500 _92 (per task brief) reported 3-4x with 279->39 FS.

practical_guidance.pursue: Short-horizon (5d-10d) up-move cells on large US universes (sp500 > russell1000 ~ nasdaq) are reliably discriminating with strong top-tail concentration. Higher thresholds (+20%, +40%) trade base rate for lift and remain discriminating on test. These are the cells worth productionizing.
practical_guidance.avoid_or_caution: Long horizons (>=25d) at the +10% threshold decay toward null on the recent test window despite decent eval AUC — do not trust eval AUC alone for these. H>=50 needs a test-split redesign before it is evaluable. The 100d/+10% cell is effectively unusable under the current split.
practical_guidance.expectations: A data scientist should expect: (1) eval AUC over-states test AUC by 0.02-0.14, worse the longer the horizon; (2) ranking (R-precision) survives prevalence drift even when calibrated-probability Brier does not — judge cells on R-precision, not Brier, under drift; (3) FS prunes hard (279 -> 25-65) on most cells with neutral-to-positive effect; (4) the strongest signal lives in the prediction-extreme top picks (P@1 descends with k on US panels).
